note: Language Lab practice settings based on the USCIS scoring guidelines for the reading and writing portions. They are NOT USCIS rules: a text comparison cannot judge pauses, pronunciation or whether an officer understands. See scoringBasis for the source and what each setting stands for.

scoringBasis.source: USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 12, Part E, Chapter 2 (English and Civics Testing), Reading Test and Writing Test
scoringBasis.fromTheGuidelines: Read all content words; short words may be omitted; omitting or substituting a content word fails; pronunciation errors that do not interfere with the meaning are fine (reading). Spelling, capitalization and omitted short words do not fail unless they interfere with the meaning; a different sentence or different words fail (writing).
languageLabChoices: Short words are the 'Other (Function)' words of the two official vocabulary lists (the manual does not define them): a, and, during, for, here, in, of, on, the, to, we. They may be missing or added.
Words must be in order (the manual does not mention order).
A plural or possessive ending (-s, -es, 's) is the same word.
One extra content word is allowed (an inserted word is not listed as a failure, and a recogniser can add one).
Writing only: a one-letter spelling error in a word of 5+ letters counts, unless the typed word is itself a different word of the official vocabulary.
scoringBasis.notScored: Pauses, pronunciation and whether an officer would understand cannot be judged from text.
